## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

<!-- This is a famous expression.
When they manage to print "Hello world" on the output of a console.
It also shows that one has mastered one of the most basic thing and successful managed to instruct the computer. -->

While numbers are natural (extension of a calculator), texts is a different type object. And at first it is unclear why do we need it!!! For our case, this essentially allows us to store qualitative variable. It is called strings or character

And to tell R that it is a character we wrap it within quotation marks @fig-completion.

Like numbers and integers, it is natural to do operation @sec-arithmetic, for boolean type @sec-boolean, there are also specific symbol to make operation @sec-boolean-operation. However, there are no obvious way/mathematically derived of doing operation. Instead we manipulate them, combine, cut, remove letters etc... As such manipulating is more done through function @sec-functionCoding and there is no dedicated new symbols.

Note that a computer is not aware of the content! So "Magadascar" is the sequence of letters and is different from "Madagascar". As 12 is different from 21. While the latter is easy to separate, it is not easy to differentiate the latter. These typos are common when you enter data or naming a variable.

## Examples {.unnumbered}

This is a example of operation where we combine two text together


```{r}
paste("Hello", "world", sep = " ")

paste("Hello", "world", sep = " there ")

paste("Hello", "world", "life", sep = " there ")

word1 <- "Hello"
word2 <- "world"

paste(word1, word2)
```


```{r}
#| echo: true

## see the difference among these three

sin #the name of an object
sin() # the function sinus
"sin" # a text composed of three letters s



```
